extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of art history, artists, and scholars interested in Giotto and early Renaissance painting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative observations about the qualities, techniques, materials, design, and conservation of Giotto's paintings and related works (fresco, panel, mosaic, architectural ornament). Intended to identify what makes his works excellent and what practical choices affect durability and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence of execution / freshness over time
rubrics_metrics.description: "wrought with so great diligence that up to our own day they have remained fresh."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meticulous, careful execution preserves the visual freshness of a work across centuries; attention to technique and materials at time of making contributes strongly to long-term appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful portraiture / life-likeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Portraits described as "very well made" (e.g., portrait of Giotto himself; Messer Farinata degli Uberti); painted likenesses of patrons and notable persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate likeness and convincing individual characterization are valued—portraits 'from the life' are praised and collected; portrait quality can determine a work's esteem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression of inner feeling and devotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Paintings like S. Francis receiving the Stigmata are praised as "so loving and devout" and showing "a most ardent desire" and "infinite love".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conveying spiritual or emotional states (devotion, ardour, grief) through pose, face, and composition is a major criterion for excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and novelty of landscape elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of "landscapes full of trees and cliffs, which was something new in those times."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introducing natural landscape settings into narrative scenes is an innovative compositional choice that enriches narrative and was judged positively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative completeness and episodic scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels described as containing "three very beautiful scenes of the life of the same Saint."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-structured multi-scene compositions that tell several moments of a life or story coherently are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fresco groundwork and material choices for durability (intonaco)
rubrics_metrics.description: He "caused to be made over the whole surface ... an intonaco or incrustation--with lime, gypsum, and powdered brick all mixed together" so the pictures "have been preserved up to the present day."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice and preparation of the plaster ground (intonaco) is crucial for fresco preservation; specific mixes can prolong life but may have long-term drawbacks (see next criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of material limitations and long-term corrosion
rubrics_metrics.description: Warning that "the negligence of those who should have taken care of them had not allowed them to be much injured by the damp" and that "the nature of gypsum, when it has been mixed with lime, is to corrode in time and to grow rotten ... spoils the colours."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoiding certain material combinations or ensuring maintenance against damp is necessary; practitioners should be aware that some mixes (e.g., gypsum+lime) may initially bind well but later damage pigments and plaster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalistic gesture and small-detail realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures praised for precise, telling gestures (e.g., a man-servant "chasing the flies" while "holding his nose in disgust").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small, natural gestures and everyday details make characters believable and communicate narrative/character effectively; these are hallmark traits of superior painting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drapery modelling and natural flow of folds
rubrics_metrics.description: "The draperies are wrought to such a degree of softness" and elsewhere "a natural flow of folds."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soft, convincing rendering of cloth and folds that follows the body and movement enhances realism and is highly prized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreshortening and early perspective techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: "The foreshortenings ... are very worthy of praise and should be held in great price among craftsmen" and are described as 'the first beginning and method of making them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective foreshortening and experimental perspective that convincingly depict depth and body in space are important technical achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping, composition, and unity of light and shadow
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise for "grouping of the Apostles, who are travailing in diverse manners" and the difficulty of achieving "a unity such as that which is seen in the lights and shadows of so great a sail" in mosaic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cohesive groupings and a unified treatment of light and shadow across figures and elements create powerful, integrated compositions—this applies across media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision of draftsmanship / measured proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: Anecdote: Giotto drew "a circle, so true in proportion and circumference that to behold it was a marvel."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical precision in drawing and proportion (clean contours, accurate geometry) is an admired aspect of mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conveying moral or allegorical content by pose and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples like the gesture toward usurers that shows "contempt of money" and the personification of "human avarice and greed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gestures, facial expression, and composition to embody abstract qualities (virtues/vices) so that moral meaning is clear and potent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventiveness and original iconographic ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenes (e.g., Apocalypse) are noted as possibly "inventions of Dante" and Giotto's works are repeatedly praised for new and beautiful ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original conceptual invention and novel iconography distinguish eminent works; borrowing or transformation of literary ideas into visual form is a mark of creativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate scale and monumentality
rubrics_metrics.description: Works cited include an Angel "seven braccia high" and a Crucifix "larger than life," demonstrating scale choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing an appropriate scale (monumental or intimate) for subject and location contributes to the work's impact; large-scale works require different technical and compositional planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapting technique to medium constraints (mosaic, distemper, fresco)
rubrics_metrics.description: Navicella mosaic: difficulty in achieving unity with pieces of glass; panel works in distemper; fresco scenes on walls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists must adapt compositional, color, and lighting strategies to the peculiar constraints and possibilities of each medium to attain unity and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful planning, modelling, and marking for architectural ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: Giotto "designed all the scenes ... and marked out the model with white, black, and red colours in all those places wherein the marbles and the friezes were to go, with much diligence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed preparatory models, colour-marking, and careful layout are essential when integrating painted ornament with architecture and sculpture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of design across disciplines (sculpture, relief, painting, architecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Giotto made models and scenes "in marble wherein are the beginnings of all the arts, in sculpture and in relief"—design and invention are the parents of the arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful monumental projects often require coherent design that coordinates painting with sculpture and architectural form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of iconography and symbolic program
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Commune painting he placed Justice, Strength, Wisdom, and Temperance as appropriate accompanying Virtues—"characteristic and appropriate in invention."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject choices and symbolic accompaniments must suit the function and audience of the work; appropriate allegorical programs enhance meaning and reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation, restoration history, and vulnerability to damage
rubrics_metrics.description: Many works "have been restored by others ... destroyed or removed" and suffered from "damp" leading to blackened flesh-colours and peeled intonaco.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should consider restoration history and environmental vulnerability; makers should choose materials and sites to minimize long-term deterioration and advocate for maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chiaroscuro and highlight technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings "in water-colour, outlined with the pen, in chiaroscuro, with the high lights in white" are singled out as marvels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skilled use of chiaroscuro and selective highlights to model form is a technical criterion demonstrating mastery of light, shade, and three-dimensionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressive heads, vivacity, and characterisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Praises such as "grace and vivacity of the heads, which are miraculous" and that every figure 'shows very great craftsmanship' in attitude and expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liveliness and distinctive facial characterization across multiple figures are indicators of high artistic quality.
